problem: The free PDF and follow-up selfscan are publicly live, but the workbook landing routes visitors through a second diagnostic page to discover the actual 30-minute appointment calendar. This adds unnecessary steps for high-intent buyers who already want to talk.
root_cause: The landing offered a /frisse-blik explainer rather than the existing active Calendly booking URL for the 30-minute advice event. First-party CTA clicks alone cannot prove booked meetings.
fix: Preserve the ungated PDF and existing selfscan CTA; replace only the landing's optional secondary Frisse Blik explainer CTA with the actual verified active free Calendly appointment type. Mark it booking-page *intent*, never booked-call conversion.
prevention: Free PDF and selfscan remain ungated and primary.
Existing verified Calendly scheduling URL reused, no new event, scheduling automation or lead form.
Never count an outbound click as a booked call or received revenue.
Preserve privacy controls and existing first-party click tracker.
No invented scarcity, testimonials, paid results or provider permissions.

evidence.provider_proof: Active personal 30-minute no-charge event; 142 open time slots available between 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-22 in provider query (dynamic, not guaranteed).

outcome: Candidate lower-friction voluntary booking intent; no new human lead, appointment, completed session or paid order is implied. Only provider booking receipt can prove appointment.
